chapters.summary: Yuddha: Vibhishana takes refuge with Rama, the vanaras build the setu, Agastya teaches the Aditya-hridaya, Ravana falls, and Rama is crowned in Ayodhya.

cmds.say: The vanara army covers the southern shore like a second ocean. Hanuman and you stand again with your companions.
Rama, Lakshmana, Sugriva and Jambavan rejoin your party!
Lanka lies across the water. Now we must find a way over it.

cmds.objective: Speak with the stranger on the beach, to the east.

cmds.say: Supplies for the army! Fruit, roots, honey and herbs.
I am Nila, commander of the vanaras. Every soldier is ready, and every heart is with Rama.

then.say: He has come from our enemy. Let Rama test him first.

then.objective: Return to Vibhishana and hear what Rama decides.

then.say: A rakshasa among us! But if Rama trusts him, so do I.

else.say: Hanuman, they say you set Lanka ablaze with your own tail! Tell me everything later.

then.say: We carried mountains! My arms will ache for a year.

else.say: Boulders, trees, whole hillsides! We are ready to carry anything Nala asks for.

then.say: Vibhishana waits. First ask Angada for his counsel.

cmds.say: A rakshasa descends from the sky with four companions and stands in the air above the beach. The vanaras raise rocks and trees.
I am Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother. I begged him to return Sita, and he shamed me before his whole court.

then.say: I warned him: people who say only pleasant things are easy to find. One who says what is hard but good is rare.
Long ago, when Ravana planned to carry Sita away, Maricha said almost the same words to him.
Two counsellors gave Ravana the same advice. He listened to neither.

cmds.say: I have left Lanka, my home and my family. I seek refuge with Rama.
Do not trust him, friend! He is the enemy's own brother. He may be a spy.

then.say: Rama turns to his counsellors: "What do you say?"

cmds.say: He spoke for Sita in Ravana's court. He saved my life when Ravana ordered my death.

then.choice: Rama turns to you: "{player}, what does he ask of us?"

options.label: Refuge. He asks for your protection.

then.say: I know who he is, child. I asked what he wants.
From Lanka, yes. But what does he ask for?
Yes. He asks for refuge.

cmds.say: Rama listens to every counsel. Then he speaks.
Even if Ravana himself came seeking refuge, I would not turn him away. I give {w:abhaya} to all who come to me. That is my {w:vrata}.

onCorrect.say: Right. This is Rama's vow of refuge, and the source of his fearlessness.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Tap the word card and read the gloss, then try it in battle.

then.say: Go, bring him to me. Say my vow to him.
Vibhishana hears the vow and comes down from the sky.

cmds.say: Vibhishana bows at Rama's feet. Rama sprinkles him with sea water and names him king of Lanka.
Sugriva embraces Vibhishana. 'Then you are my friend too. Walk at Rama's side; I will lead the vanara army from the front.'
Sugriva goes to command the army. He will fight beside you on the battlefield.
Vibhishana joins your party!

cmds.objective: Ask Nala, by the shore, how to cross the ocean.

then.say: The setu is finished. Cross it, and may your feet be swift.
Rama prayed to the Ocean for three days. When the Ocean did not answer, Rama took up his bow in anger.
Then the Ocean rose in person and bowed. 'Nala, son of Vishvakarma, can build a bridge. I will hold up whatever he places on my waters.'
For five days the vanaras uproot trees and carry rocks. Nala sets them in the sea, and they float.
Let every stone sit true. Then the bridge will reach Lanka.
Fourteen yojanas on the first day; then twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two and twenty-three. A hundred yojanas in all.
On the fifth day the setu stretches all the way to Lanka. The gods watch from the sky in wonder.

then.objective: Cross the setu south to Lanka.

else.say: Rama will tell us when to begin. First, see who has come to the beach.

cmds.say: The ocean stretches endlessly. The bridge is not built yet.
The bridge Nala built stretches a hundred yojanas across the waves. The vanara army pours across it, roaring Rama's name.
Small islets dot the way. Rakshasa scouts may lurk in their grass.

cmds.objective: Cross the setu south to Suvela hill.

cmds.say: Sit with us a while! We carried the stones for this bridge with our own hands.
Your party is fully rested.
The army camps on {n:place.suvela_camp} hill. From its slopes you can see Lanka's golden walls, lit by a thousand torches.

cmds.objective: Prepare at the camp, then speak with Angada.

then.say: Ravana chose war. The army marches through the south pass whenever you are ready.

else.say: Rama sent me to Ravana's court with one last offer: return Sita, and live in peace.
Ravana laughed and called for my capture. I leapt up and broke the top of his palace tower as I left!
There is no other way now. Lanka's gates open onto the battlefield, just south of here.

else.objective: March south to the battlefield before Lanka.

cmds.say: Even an army needs honey and herbs. Buy what you need.
This shrine has stood on Suvela since before Lanka was built. Rest and recite here whenever you need.

then.say: The battlefield lies south. Be careful out there.

else.say: Nobody marches until Angada returns from Ravana's court.

cmds.say: Every vanara and every bear is ready. When the gates open, I will be at the front of the army.
Rest at the shrine first, friend. The battle ahead will be long.

then.say: I was on the beach when Rama made his vow. Whoever comes to him even once and says 'I am yours' is safe from every creature.
{w:abhaya}: freedom from fear. That is why a rakshasa walks in our camp now, and nobody minds.

cmds.say: Look at Lanka's walls. Tomorrow we will be at its gates.
A bear warrior of Jambavan's clan. 'Our king is old, but he still fights like a mountain.'
Wait for Angada's word. He went as Rama's envoy to Ravana's court.
The gates of Lanka open, and Ravana's armies pour out. The battle of Lanka begins.
The vanara physician Sushena tends the wounded behind the lines. Rest with him between battles.

cmds.objective: Break through Ravana's generals to the city gate in the south.

cmds.say: The rakshasas fight with illusions, but Rama's arrows cut through them all!
I am Sushena, physician of the vanaras. Lie down; these herbs will restore you.
Your party is fully rested.

else.say: When Lakshmana fell to Indrajit's weapon, Hanuman flew to the Himalaya and carried back a whole mountain of healing herbs.
One sprig of the life-giving herb is left. Keep it for the darkest hour.

cmds.say: Dhumraksha, Smoke-Eyed, one of Ravana's fiercest generals, blocks the way with a great iron club.
Monkeys and men against Lanka? I will scatter you like dust!

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

onWin.say: Hanuman's blow ends Dhumraksha's charge. His army flees back toward the walls.

onWin.objective: Press on south toward the city gate.

cmds.say: The ground shakes. Kumbhakarna, Ravana's giant brother, has been woken from his long sleep.
Even he told Ravana that taking Sita was wrong. Yet he fights for his brother.
Brother, you did wrong. But I will not abandon you.

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

onWin.say: Rama's arrows bring the giant down at last. Kumbhakarna falls like a mountain, and the earth trembles.
In Lanka, Ravana weeps for his brother.

then.say: Then Indrajit strikes from the clouds with Brahma's weapon. Rama, Lakshmana and the army fall senseless.
Old Jambavan, wounded too, sends Hanuman north to the mountain of herbs.

onWin.objective: Press on south toward the city gate.

cmds.say: Indrajit, Ravana's son, who once defeated Indra himself, fights hidden inside clouds of illusion.
Fight me if you can. No one can strike what they cannot see!

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

then.say: Lakshmana takes up one last arrow and makes a vow.

else.say: Lakshmana looses a final arrow with a vow: 'If Rama is truthful and devoted to dharma, let this arrow strike.'

onWin.say: The arrow flies true, and Indrajit's sorcery ends forever.
Before the gate of Lanka stands a small, radiant sage. He seems to have been waiting for you.

onWin.objective: Speak with the sage before the gate.

else.say: Ravana himself is coming out to fight. Rama stands weary, thinking of the battle ahead.
The sage Agastya, who has come with the gods to watch the battle, approaches Rama.
Rama, mighty-armed, hear the eternal secret by which you will conquer every foe in battle.
It is the {n:move.aditya_hrdaya}, the hymn to the heart of the Sun. It destroys all enemies and brings victory.

onCorrect.say: Well done. You read the hymn's grammar like a true student of Agastya.

onWrong.say: Not quite. Find the verb first; the other words arrange themselves around it.

else.say: Agastya also blesses Rama's greatest weapon, the {n:move.brahmastra}, so that it will not fail.

then.say: The hymn shines gold in your verse book. Go, Rama. Victory is yours.

else.choice: Recite the hymn with Agastya now?

else.say: Rest, and come back to me. Ravana's palace will not open until the hymn is whole.
Recite it three times, and you will win.

then.say: The hymn blazes gold, bright as the rising sun. Rama's strength returns.
Agastya blesses Rama and departs as quietly as he came.

then.objective: Enter Ravana's palace through the city gate in the south.

else.say: Almost. Breathe, child, and recite with me again when you are ready.

then.say: The gate will not yield. Agastya's hymn must be restored first. Speak with the sage.

else.say: Ravana's generals still hold the field. Break through them first.

cmds.say: Ravana, ten-headed king of Lanka, rises from his throne. Indra's charioteer Matali brings a chariot from heaven for Rama.
You have killed my brother and my sons. Now you will face me.
Return Sita, even now, and live.
Never!

then.say: Matali, the charioteer of the gods, whispers to Rama: when Ravana's strength wanes, loose Brahma's weapon.

cmds.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

onWin.say: Rama looses the brahmastra that Agastya blessed. It strikes Ravana's heart, and the ten-headed king falls.
The gods rain flowers from the sky. Vibhishana kneels beside his brother and weeps.
Should I perform the rites for one who did such wrong?
Rama answers him gently: all {w:vaira} ends with death.
Then I will give my brother his last rites, with honour.
Vibhishana was crowned king of Lanka, and Sita and Rama were together again at last.
Then Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and all their friends boarded the flying chariot Pushpaka and rose into the sky, toward Ayodhya.

then.say: From the Pushpaka, Rama shows Sita the places of their story.

then.choice: Rama asks you: "Where did we hear this verse?"

then.say: Not there. Look down again.

then.choice: Rama asks you: "Where did we hear this verse?"

then.say: Not there. Look down again.

then.choice: Rama asks you: "Where did we hear this verse?"

then.say: Not there. Look down again.

then.choice: Rama asks you: "Where did we hear this verse?"

then.say: Not there. Look down again.

then.choice: Rama asks you: "Where did we hear this verse?"

then.say: Not there. Look down again.

onWin.say: Fourteen years have passed. In {n:place.ayodhya_return}, Bharata comes out to meet his brother, carrying the sandals he kept on the throne all this time.

then.say: Bharata places the sandals on Rama's feet and bows to him.

onWin.say: Ayodhya is lit with lamps and garlands, and every street is full of joy.

onWin.objective: Go north to the coronation in the palace courtyard.

then.say: The coronation is done. Go home, child; your teacher is waiting.

else.say: The day has come. Let Rama be crowned king of Ayodhya.
Vasishtha pours the sacred waters. Rama sits on the throne with Sita beside him.
Shatrughna holds the white royal umbrella, and Sugriva and Vibhishana wave the fans. Lakshmana and Bharata stand close by.
Sita takes a pearl necklace from her own neck and gives it to Hanuman, the friend who found her.
Rama ruled for many years, and in his kingdom no one knew fear, sickness or sorrow.
The verse book glows in your hands. Its pages are full again. It is time to return to your teacher.
You are back on the banks of the Tamasa. Morning light falls on the ashrama.

cmds.say: You walked the whole way with us, reciter. Thank you.
Tell your teacher our story, child. Tell it truly.
I only kept the throne warm. These sandals ruled Ayodhya for fourteen years.
My son is home. There is nothing more I could ask for.
All I want is to serve Rama, for as long as his story is told.
Fourteen years in the forest, and every day of it by my brother's side.
Who would have thought it, on that hill by Lake Pampa? A friend, a kingdom, and now this day.
The lamps! The whole city is lit for Rama's return!
Did you see the flying chariot land? It shone like the sun!
I lit twelve lamps all by myself!
So this is Ayodhya! The fruit here is almost as sweet as in Kishkindha.

then.say: The story lives in you now. Recite it well, and recite it often.

else.say: You have returned, {player}. And the verse book is whole again.

then.choice: Valmiki asks: "With whom did you walk, child?"

options.label: With Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman.

then.say: Lanka is so far! But with whom did you walk?

else.say: You walked beside Rama from the Tamasa to Lanka and home again. You heard the verses where they were first spoken.
When I first saw the krauncha bird fall, my grief became a verse. Now you have carried every verse home.
Thank you, my student. Because of you, this story can be told for all time.

then.say: Kusha and Lava, two boys of this ashrama, have learned my whole story.
Go with them to Ayodhya, and sing it before Rama.
The twins sing in the streets of Ayodhya. Rama hears them and brings them into his palace.
Rama sits on his throne. His brothers and ministers are with him.
Brothers, listen. These two sing a great story.
{player}, sing with them: say one line in every book.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Kusha and Lava sing.
Rama listens with his brothers. His whole mind is on the story.
As long as there are mountains and rivers, Rama's story will live.

else.say: Let us begin again, from the very first word. Teach it to the next student who comes.

cmds.say: Behind the rocks lies a supply chest the rakshasas left behind. It holds healing herbs.
You found 2 healing herbs.
Ravana's spies see everything! Not one of you will reach Suvela!

battle.intro: A rakshasa scout leaps out of the islet grass!

onWin.say: The scout dives into the sea and swims for Lanka. He has left his honey behind.

then.say: Kusha and Lava sing.
